title: Show the error messages from the system journal since this boot
summary: Read the system log for the current boot, keep only the lines that mention a word you choose, and show the last few. Use it to find out why a service or a device misbehaves.

aliases.text: find error in system logs this boot

steps.explain: Show the most recent error-level messages of the current boot. -b selects this boot, -p err keeps priority error and worse, and tail keeps the last 20 lines.
steps.expect: Lines such as 'Nov 12 10:01:02 myhost kernel: ...' with the time, host, program and message.

steps.explain: Search the whole boot log for a word, ignoring case. grep -i matches upper and lower case, and tail keeps the last 20 matches.
steps.expect: Matching log lines from this boot. No output means nothing in this boot mentions the word.

steps.explain: Count which program logs the most matches. awk prints the program name in field 5 and removes the [pid] part and the colon after it, sort and uniq -c count, sort -nr lists the biggest count first.
steps.cmd: journalctl -b --no-pager | grep -i '<WORD>' | awk '{sub(/[:\[].*/, "", $5); print $5}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 10
steps.expect: Lines such as '  14 bluetoothd': the count first, then the program name.
